verses.text: Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them there to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and the guardians raising Ahab's sons.
The letters said, “Your master's sons are with you, and you have chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons. As soon as you get this letter,
pick the best and most qualified of your master's sons, put him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's family.”
They were terrified. “Two kings couldn't stand against him,” they said. “How can we?”

The palace administrator, the city governor, the elders, and the guardians sent this reply to Jehu: “We're your servants and will do whatever you tell us. We won't make anyone king. Do what you think is best.”

Jehu wrote them a second letter: “If you're on my side and will obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow.” The seventy princes were in the care of the leading men of the city who were raising them.
When the letter arrived, they took all seventy of the king's sons and killed them. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu in Jezreel.
A messenger told him, “They've brought the heads of the king's sons.” He answered, “Put them in two piles at the city gate and leave them there until morning.”
The next morning Jehu went out and stood before all the people. “You're innocent,” he said. “I plotted against my master and killed him, but who killed all these?
You can be sure that nothing the LORD said about Ahab's family will fail to happen. The LORD has done what he said through his servant Elijah.”
Jehu struck down everyone left from Ahab's house in Jezreel, along with his leading men, close friends, and priests, until no one was left.
Then he set out for Samaria. On the road, at the shepherds' shearing house,
he met relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah. “Who are you?” he asked. They said, “We're Ahaziah's relatives. We're going down to greet the children of the king and the queen.”
“Take them alive,” he ordered. His men seized all forty-two and killed them at the pit by the shearing house. He left none of them alive.

After leaving there, Jehu met Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and asked, “Are you with me as I'm with you?” Jehonadab said, “I am.” “Then give me your hand,” Jehu replied. Jehonadab did, and Jehu pulled him into the chariot.
“Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD,” Jehu said, and he took Jehonadab along in his chariot.
When Jehu arrived in Samaria, he struck down everyone left of Ahab's family there until he'd destroyed them all, just as the LORD had told Elijah.
Jehu gathered the people and said, “Ahab served Baal a little. Jehu will serve him much more.

Call all Baal's prophets, all his worshipers, and all his priests. Nobody may miss this. I have a great sacrifice to offer Baal. Whoever stays away will die.” Jehu was deceiving them because he meant to destroy Baal's worshipers.
He said, “Set apart a solemn assembly for Baal!” So they announced it.
Jehu sent word throughout Israel, and every one of Baal's worshipers came. They went into Baal's temple and filled it from one end to the other.
He told the keeper of the wardrobe, “Bring out robes for all Baal's worshipers,” and the keeper brought them out.
Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered Baal's temple. Jehu told Baal's worshipers, “Look around and make sure none of the LORD's servants are here with you. Only Baal's worshipers should be here.”

They went in to make sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and warned them, “If any of the men I put in your hands gets away, whoever lets him go will pay with his own life.”

As soon as the burnt offering was finished, Jehu ordered the guards and officers, “Go in and kill them. Let no one escape.” They struck the worshipers down with their swords and threw the bodies out. Then they went to the inner shrine of Baal's temple.
They took the sacred pillars out of Baal's temple and burned them.
They tore down Baal's pillar and demolished his temple. They turned the site into a latrine, and it remains one to this day.
That's how Jehu put an end to Baal worship in Israel.
But Jehu held on to the sins Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel into, worshiping the gold calves at Bethel and Dan.
The LORD told Jehu, “You did what was right in my eyes and carried out everything I intended for Ahab's family. Your descendants will sit on Israel's throne through the fourth generation.”
Yet Jehu didn't take care to follow the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with his whole heart. He kept on with the sins Jeroboam had led Israel into.
In those days the LORD began cutting away parts of Israel's territory. Hazael attacked Israel all along its borders,
east of the Jordan, throughout Gilead and the territories of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh. That included all Gilead and Bashan, starting at Aroer beside the Arnon valley.
The rest of Jehu's acts, everything he did, and the power he showed are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehu died and joined his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz became king in his place.
Jehu ruled over Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.
